arXiv:2604.24859v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Fractional Chern insulators (FCIs) are zero magnetic field analogs of fractional quantum Hall states. item.title: Impact of current-induced magnons on spin-orbit torque analysis
item.description:
📚 arXiv
👤 Tamás Prok, Jan Hidding, Szabolcs Csonka, Péter Makk, Marcos H. D. Guimarães, Endre Tóvári
arXiv:2504.16661v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: The second-harmonic Hall technique is a widely used, sensitive method for studying the spin-orbit torques generated by charge current. It exploits the dependence of the Hall resistance on the magnetization direction, although thermal phenomena also contribute. Historically, deviations from the expected magnetic field dependence have usually been neglected. Based on our studies on permalloy/platinum bilayers, we show that a counterpart to the magnon-related spin-flip unidirectional magnetoresistance - known to appear in the second-harmonic longitudinal resistance - appears in the Hall data, and that describing the results in a wide field range with these contributions is essential to accurately estimate the torques.

item.description:

arXiv:2511.00813v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We explore the role of interfacial Rashba spin-orbit coupling (SOC) for the Josephson diode effect in all-metal diffusive Josephson junctions. Devices with Fe/Pt and Cu/Pt weak links between Nb leads reveal a Josephson diode effect in an in-plane magnetic field with magneto-chiral anisotropy according to the point symmetry of Rashba SOC. The Rashba SOC originates from inversion symmetry breaking at the metal-metal interfaces. A control sample with a plain Cu-layer as weak link, in contrast, exhibits an axis-symmetric diode effect. The Fraunhofer patterns display an apparent inverted hysteresis which can be traced back to stray fields resulting from the conventional hysteretic vortex pinning in the Nb contacts.
